currentContext.business: Gujarat Terce Laboratories markets branded pharmaceutical formulations in India across paediatrics, gynaecology and women's health, and physician and general medicine, spanning 10 therapeutic areas, 125 products and about 50 brands, of which 14 (the 'Fantastic 14') and 32 SKUs are designated focus items. The Company does not manufacture in-house: it operates a deliberate contract-manufacturing model in which long-term partners that are WHO-GMP certified and internationally accredited produce the goods, while all formulations, trade names and product specifications vest with Gujarat Terce and an independent in-house quality-assurance team audits partner plants and signs off every batch before dispatch. Demand is generated by a field force calling on doctors, with product reaching patients through a stockist and retail-pharmacy chain of 385 stockists and over 22,000 retail outlets fed from the Chhatral Mother Warehouse in Gandhinagar.

currentContext.expansion: Gujarat Terce runs a deliberately asset-light model and the routed text describes no manufacturing capex or plant project for FY26 or FY27. Manufacturing is done entirely by long-term contract partners that are WHO-GMP certified and internationally accredited, and the Company states the model is scalable with 'capacity addition without fixed capital deployment' - so incremental volume is added through partner plants rather than through its own capital spend, with partner plants chosen for proximity to the Chhatral Mother Warehouse, Gandhinagar, to minimise freight cost and inbound lead times. The only physical-asset milestones in the bundle are historical, placed in the 2010s: WHO-GMP certification at the Chhatral manufacturing facility, ISO 9001 obtained, and a cephalosporin unit commissioned. What the Company is actually expanding is commercial reach and field capability rather than capacity: the BREAKOUT programme, initiated in FY23-25 with portfolio rationalisation, field restructuring and financial discipline, delivered a return to profitability, near-zero debt and a second consecutive year of positive operating cash flow in FY26, and FY27 is designated BREAKOUT Year 3, the growth-execution phase. Nineteen headquarters across India, from Orai in the Lucknow region to Burhanpur in the Indore region, beat their FY26 targets under the BREAKOUT HQ programme, and management intends to scale that programme to build more pockets of excellence across the country, alongside a new FY27 incentive system tied to headquarters productivity, brand results and doctor conversion, and deeper field training. Distribution infrastructure already spans 385 stockists and over 22,000 retail outlets serving around 25,000 doctors across 13 states. Financing-side, the only capital event disclosed is the Managing Director's conversion of warrants in December 2025 and February 2026 at a premium of Rs 37.70 over the market price, with 3,71,000 shares allotted and listed on the BSE on 25 February 2026, taking promoter holding to 40.03%.
